concepts.title: The estimation problem
concepts.blurb: A hidden state $x_t$ evolves by linear dynamics $x_{t+1}=Fx_t+w_t$ with process noise $w_t\sim\mathcal{N}(0,Q)$; only a noisy projection $y_t=Hx_t+v_t$, $v_t\sim\mathcal{N}(0,R)$ is observed. The task is the posterior $p(x_t\mid y_{1:t})$ — under linear-Gaussian assumptions it stays Gaussian forever, so tracking the mean and covariance is exact rather than a moment approximation.

concepts.title: Bayesian fusion of two Gaussians
concepts.blurb: Two independent Gaussian estimates $\mathcal{N}(\mu_1,\sigma_1^2)$ and $\mathcal{N}(\mu_2,\sigma_2^2)$ of the same scalar combine into a third Gaussian whose precision is the sum: $1/\sigma^2 = 1/\sigma_1^2 + 1/\sigma_2^2$, $\mu = \sigma^2(\mu_1/\sigma_1^2 + \mu_2/\sigma_2^2)$. The narrower estimate dominates; the posterior is sharper than either input. This precision-weighted mean is the entire Bayesian content of the Kalman update — everything else is bookkeeping.

concepts.title: The 1D Kalman cycle — predict and update
concepts.blurb: Discrete-time scalar dynamics $x_{t+1}=ax_t+w_t$, observation $y_t=x_t+v_t$. Each step is two moves: the predict step pushes the mean through $a$ and inflates the variance by $a^2\sigma^2+q$; the update step does Gaussian fusion against the observation, shrinking variance back. Variance reaches a steady state once predict-inflation balances update-shrinkage — the fixed point of a one-step Riccati recurrence.

concepts.title: Vector form and the covariance ellipse
concepts.blurb: In $\mathbb{R}^n$ the state covariance $\Sigma_t$ is an ellipse $\{x:x^\top\Sigma_t^{-1}x=1\}$. Prediction evolves it as $\Sigma_{t+1\mid t} = F\Sigma_{t\mid t}F^\top + Q$ — rotation, stretch, then puff up by process noise. Update collapses it along the directions $H$ observes: $\Sigma_{t\mid t} = (I-K_tH)\Sigma_{t\mid t-1}$. The covariance is a moving rigid-plus-noise picture of how confident the filter is along each direction in state space.

concepts.title: The Kalman gain as optimal mixing
concepts.blurb: The gain $K_t = \Sigma_{t\mid t-1}H^\top(H\Sigma_{t\mid t-1}H^\top+R)^{-1}$ is exactly the value that minimises the trace of the posterior covariance — equivalently, the MAP estimate, MMSE estimate, and weighted-least-squares solution all agree under the linear-Gaussian assumption. Large $R$ (noisy sensor) pulls $K$ toward $0$ and the filter trusts its prediction; small $R$ (sharp sensor) pulls $K$ toward $H^{-1}$ and the filter snaps to the measurement.

concepts.title: Tracking a 2D moving target
concepts.blurb: A constant-velocity model in the plane has state $(p_x,p_y,v_x,v_y)$ with $F$ a block-upper-triangular shear and $Q$ injecting noise into the velocity components. Observing position only ($H=[I_2\;0]$) lets the filter infer velocity from the way successive position errors correlate — the off-diagonal blocks of $\Sigma_t$ encode that inference, which is why a Kalman tracker beats every position-only smoother.
